name: Kumkumadi oil

lead: Kumkumadi Taila is a classical Ayurvedic facial oil, traditionally used as a routine skincare product to enhance the complexion. Saffron is the namesake ingredient.
People use it for a brighter, more even-looking face. A 2026 exploratory study of 30 adults measured changes in melanin index, redness, hydration and elasticity over 15 days.

paras: In the study the oil was applied once daily to the face with a standardised massage followed by washing off. Commercial products are used as a daily or evening facial oil.
No adverse events were reported in the 15-day study, and barrier measures (transepidermal water loss) did not change. As with any oil, individual reactions are possible.

angle.text: People use the oil to even out and brighten the complexion. In the one instrument-based study, melanin and redness readings fell and hydration and elasticity rose over 15 days.

lead: Kumkumadi Taila (kumkumadi tailam) is a classical Ayurvedic facial oil traditionally used as a routine preventive skincare product to enhance the complexion.[1] Chemical analysis of the studied oil identified compounds including safranal, berberine, retinol and sesamin, which the authors link to antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and pigmentation-modulating actions reported in the literature.[1]

In a single-arm 15-day exploratory study of 30 healthy adults with Fitzpatrick skin types III-IV, daily facial application produced statistically significant changes in melanin index, erythema index, hydration and elasticity.[1] A separate registered trial of a 'Vasu Facial Beauty Oil' in 32 people, covering wrinkles, dry skin and pigment, is listed as completed.[2]

paras: Traditionally it is applied to the face as preventive skincare to improve complexion.[1]

A 2026 single-arm study in Frontiers in Medicine applied the oil once daily for 15 days with a standardised massage and wash-off, measuring skin with a DermaLab Combo device at baseline, day 7 and day 15.[1] Melanin index, erythema index, hydration and elasticity changed significantly; transepidermal water loss and skin thickness did not, which the authors read as short-term cosmetic improvement without barrier disruption.[1] No adverse events were reported.[1] The study had no control group. A trial of Vasu Facial Beauty Oil (NCT05646953, n=32) is registered as completed.[2]
